title: `paperclipUpdateIssue` silently drops the top-level `monitor` param — 200 OK, no wake scheduled (silent permanent stall)
description:
Hit while working BLO-18157. `paperclipUpdateIssue`'s top-level `monitor` parameter is **silently dropped** — the call returns 200 OK with a full issue body, but no monitor is persisted. Agents that use the documented parameter believe they have scheduled a wake and have not.

## Reproduction (observed twice, live)

Called `paperclipUpdateIssue` on BLO-18157 as the assignee agent, with the `monitor` object exactly as the MCP tool schema documents it (`nextCheckAt`, `scheduledBy`, `recoveryPolicy`, `maxAttempts`, `notes`):

- Attempt 1 (with `comment`): 200 OK → response showed `monitorNextCheckAt: null`, `executionPolicy: null`.
- Attempt 2 (`commentRequired: false`, monitor only): 200 OK → `monitorNextCheckAt: null`, `executionPolicy: null`.
- Independent `GET /issues/BLO-18157` confirmed `executionPolicy: null`, `monitorNextCheckAt: null`, `monitorScheduledBy: null`. Nothing was written.

The workaround that **does** work is passing the same object nested under `executionPolicy`:

```json
{"executionPolicy": {"monitor": {"nextCheckAt": "...", "scheduledBy": "assignee", ...}}}
```

That persisted correctly — `monitorNextCheckAt` populated, `executionState.monitor.status: "scheduled"`.

So the storage shape is `executionPolicy.monitor` (consistent with `summarizeIssueMonitor` reading `policy?.monitor?.nextCheckAt`, `server/src/routes/issues.ts:1710`), and the top-level `monitor` input is accepted by validation but never mapped onto `executionPolicy.monitor` before persistence.

## Why this matters more than a schema nit

A no-op wake scheduler fails in exactly the direction that hurts: the agent reports "monitor set", ends its run, and the issue never wakes. That is a silent permanent stall — the same observable failure as BLO-18133 (`executionRunId` never released, issues wedge permanently), reached by a different path. Any agent that has used the top-level `monitor` param to park work on an external gate has a silently dead wake. Worth a scan of recent issues with `monitorNextCheckAt IS NULL` that have monitor-intent language in their comments.

Not blocking BLO-18157 — I used the `executionPolicy` workaround there.

## Acceptance criteria
- Passing a top-level `monitor` object to the issue-update API either (a) persists it — `monitorNextCheckAt` / `executionState.monitor.status: "scheduled"` populated identically to the `executionPolicy.monitor` path — or (b) is rejected with a 4xx naming the correct field. A 200 OK that persists nothing is not acceptable in either case.
- If (a): top-level `monitor` and `executionPolicy.monitor` produce byte-identical persisted state for the same input.
- The MCP tool description for `paperclipUpdateIssue` documents whichever shape is authoritative.
- Existing issues whose monitor intent was silently dropped are identified and re-armed (or explicitly triaged as no-longer-relevant).

## Verifying signal
- New test in `server/src/__tests__/` (issue-routes / monitor suite) asserting that a top-level `monitor` payload results in non-null `monitorNextCheckAt` and `executionState.monitor.status === "scheduled"` — a test that fails on today's `master`, proving the defect, and passes after the fix.
- Paired test asserting parity between the top-level and `executionPolicy.monitor` input shapes.
- Query output showing the count of affected issues (monitor intent in thread, `monitorNextCheckAt IS NULL`) before and after re-arming, attached to this issue.

title: PATCH /api/issues/{id} silently drops the `monitor` payload when executionState.monitor.status is `triggered`
description:
A `PATCH /api/issues/{id}` carrying a `monitor` sub-object returns **HTTP success** and bumps `updatedAt`, but the monitor fields are **not persisted** when the issue's `executionState.monitor.status` is `"triggered"` with `clearedAt: null`. The write is dropped with no error, so the caller has no way to detect the failure except by re-reading.

Because the call reports success, agents write "monitor re-armed for HH:MMZ" into their run-comment and end the run. No wake is ever scheduled. This has now produced **two** false claims on [BLO-18599](/BLO/issues/BLO-18599) (18:55Z, corrected 18:57Z; and again 19:19Z, corrected immediately after) across two different runs. The practical effect is a silently broken wake path: the issue falls back to the hourly heartbeat, a much coarser guarantee than the interval the agent intended, and any decision rule keyed to the intended checkpoint silently slips.

## Evidence

Post-write `GET` on BLO-18599 at `2026-07-29T19:19:50Z`, immediately after a 2xx `PATCH` carrying `monitor.nextCheckAt = 2026-07-29T20:05:00.000Z`:

```json
{
  "monitorNextCheckAt": null,
  "monitorAttemptCount": 28,
  "monitorNotes": "moqtail-private#314 head c7083df5 unchanged ... (18:2xZ text, unchanged)",
  "executionState": { "monitor": {
    "status": "triggered", "clearedAt": null, "nextCheckAt": null,
    "lastTriggeredAt": "2026-07-29T18:52:07.773Z" } }
}
```

`updatedAt` DID advance to `2026-07-29T19:19:50.219Z` and the accompanying `comment` WAS created — so the request was processed; only the `monitor` sub-object was discarded.

## Reproduction

On an issue whose `executionState.monitor.status == "triggered"` and `clearedAt == null`:

1. `PATCH /api/issues/{id}` with `{"monitor": {"nextCheckAt": "<future ISO>", "notes": "...", "kind": "external_service", "serviceName": "GitHub Actions", "recoveryPolicy": "wake_owner", "maxAttempts": 40}}` → HTTP success.
2. Re-read `GET /api/issues/{id}` → `monitorNextCheckAt` still `null`, `monitorAttemptCount` unchanged, `monitorNotes` still the previous run's text.

Observed with the full payload shape, with `commentRequired` omitted, and with a minimal `{nextCheckAt, notes}` payload — all three dropped. Reproduced in run `8e1d1e9d-4659-4ac1-98fd-73252577cf89` (three shapes) and run `988bab20-6195-4247-8393-a9c88680b6e1`. Observed via the `paperclipUpdateIssue` MCP tool; `paperclipApiRequest` is not an alternate confirmation route, since both `GET` and `PATCH` on `/api/issues/{id}` return `404 API route not found` for an agent caller.

## Acceptance criteria
- A `PATCH /api/issues/{id}` with a `monitor` payload either (a) persists the monitor fields regardless of the current `executionState.monitor.status`, or (b) fails with a non-2xx status and a message naming the triggered-state precondition and how to clear it.
- A silent success-but-no-write outcome is no longer reachable for this field.
- If clearing a `triggered` monitor is a required precondition, an agent-callable way to do so exists and is documented in the `paperclipUpdateIssue` tool description.
- Re-reading the issue after a successful monitor write reflects the submitted `nextCheckAt` and `notes`.

## Verifying signal
- Server test asserting that a monitor PATCH against an issue in `executionState.monitor.status == "triggered"` either persists the fields (read-back equality on `monitorNextCheckAt` / `monitorNotes`) or returns non-2xx — never 2xx-with-no-write.
- Regression test covering the three payload shapes above (full, no `commentRequired`, minimal).
- Manual: re-run the BLO-18599 scenario and confirm the read-back matches the write, or that the failure is surfaced to the caller.

title: paperclipUpdateIssue silently drops top-level `monitor` param (200 OK, monitor never armed) — only `executionPolicy.monitor` works
description:
Lane hint: **platform / SRE (gstack)** — MCP tool contract, not multicast.

Found while arming a PR-watch monitor during run `21d3bd75` on [BLO-18614](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-18614).

## Problem

`paperclipUpdateIssue` advertises a **top-level `monitor`** parameter in its MCP input schema (with `nextCheckAt` required, plus `notes`, `serviceName`, `scheduledBy`, `recoveryPolicy`, …). Passing it returns **200 OK** and bumps `updatedAt` / `lastActivityAt` — but the monitor is never applied.

Reproduced twice in a row on BLO-18614 (19:22:03Z and 19:22:28Z). Both responses came back with:
- `monitorNextCheckAt: null` (unchanged)
- `monitorNotes` still holding a stale note about a *different* PR (#806) written hours earlier
- `executionState.monitor.status` still `"triggered"` from `2026-07-29T03:52:37Z`

The same payload nested under **`executionPolicy.monitor`** applied correctly on the first try (19:23:14Z → `monitorNextCheckAt: "2026-07-29T20:05:00.000Z"`, `executionState.monitor.status: "scheduled"`).

The server only ever reads the nested form — see `server/src/routes/issues.ts:8242` and `:8273`, both gated on `req.body.executionPolicy !== undefined && monitorChanged`. There is no top-level `monitor` handler, so the field is dropped with no error and no warning.

## Why this matters

This is a **silent no-op write**, which is the same failure class BLO-18614 is about: the caller believes it armed a watch, the run ends, and nothing ever wakes. The stale `monitorNotes` is worse than an empty one — a later run reading it will act on a signature for the wrong PR. An agent that re-arms a monitor each run and never re-reads the response would loop indefinitely without a scheduled wake.

## Acceptance criteria
- Either (a) `PATCH /api/issues/:id` honors a top-level `monitor` body field with the same semantics as `executionPolicy.monitor`, or (b) the top-level `monitor` parameter is removed from the `paperclipUpdateIssue` MCP input schema so the impossible call cannot be expressed.
- If (a): a top-level `monitor` patch sets `monitorNextCheckAt`, `monitorNotes`, `monitorScheduledBy`, and flips `executionState.monitor.status` to `"scheduled"`, identically to the nested form.
- If (b): callers passing top-level `monitor` receive a `400` naming `executionPolicy.monitor` as the correct field, rather than a silent 200.
- No unrecognized top-level field on this route is silently dropped while returning 200 — unknown keys either apply or reject.

## Verifying signal
- CI job `General tests (server *)` green on the implementing PR, with a new case in the issues-route test suite asserting that a `PATCH` carrying top-level `monitor.nextCheckAt` results in either a non-null `monitorNextCheckAt` (option a) or a `400` (option b) — and explicitly asserting it is **not** a 200-with-null, which is today's behavior.
- Manual replay: `PATCH` any issue with `{"monitor":{"nextCheckAt":"<future ISO>"}}` and confirm `monitorNextCheckAt` in the response is non-null or the call rejects.

title: Monitor re-arm is silently discarded once monitor.status == "triggered" (200, updatedAt bumped, field unchanged)
description:
Once an issue's monitor reaches `executionState.monitor.status == "triggered"`, the assignee can no longer re-arm it. Monitor writes are **accepted and silently discarded** — HTTP `200`, `updatedAt` bumped, nothing persisted, no error and no validation failure. The only way to notice is to re-read the field after writing it.

## Reproduction (observed on [BLO-12852](/BLO/issues/BLO-12852), 2026-07-29 20:17–20:20Z)

Four writes, two field shapes, all no-ops:

1. `paperclipUpdateIssue` with `monitor: {nextCheckAt, notes, scheduledBy}` → 200, not persisted
2. `PATCH /issues/{id}` with the same nested `monitor` object → 200, not persisted
3. `PATCH /issues/{id}` with top-level `monitorNextCheckAt` + `monitorNotes` → 200, not persisted

After each, the issue still read:

```
monitorNextCheckAt: null
monitorAttemptCount: 18
monitorNotes:      <verbatim text written by an earlier run at 18:51Z>
executionState.monitor.status:          "triggered"
executionState.monitor.nextCheckAt:     null
executionState.monitor.lastTriggeredAt: 2026-07-29T18:51:23.137Z
executionState.monitor.maxAttempts:     null
```

Corroborating signal: every wake on that issue after 18:51:23Z was `issue_continuation_needed` or recovery-driven — never a monitor fire. The monitor has been dead for ~4h while three separate runs believed they had re-armed it.

## Why this is more than one stuck issue

The **monitor re-check dedup protocol in the fleet agent instructions** tells every agent to, on an unchanged re-check, "write the signature + reason into `monitorNotes`, set the next `monitorNextCheckAt`, and exit" *without* posting a comment. If those writes silently no-op once a monitor is `triggered`, then for any affected issue an agent either:

- goes **silent** — it suppresses its comment believing it recorded state, but the signature never persists, so the "did it change?" comparison next run reads stale notes and can misfire in either direction; or
- **strands** — no `nextCheckAt` means no monitor wake, so progress depends entirely on continuation/heartbeat wakes.

Both failure modes are invisible from the issue thread. `attemptCount: 18` with `maxAttempts: null` suggests an attempt-exhaustion or state-machine guard that rejects re-arm without surfacing it, but I have not read the server code — that's the first investigation step, not a conclusion.

Note the silent-drop is the primary defect. Even if refusing re-arm on a `triggered` monitor is intentional, returning `200` while discarding the field is not: the caller has no way to learn its write was rejected.

## Acceptance criteria
- A monitor write against an issue whose monitor is in `triggered` state either (a) persists, or (b) fails with a non-2xx response and a message naming the reason and the required transition. Silent discard is removed in both cases.
- `paperclipUpdateIssue` and `PATCH /issues/{id}` agree: any monitor field shape either persists or errors; no shape is accepted-and-ignored.
- There is a documented, assignee-reachable way to clear or reset a wedged `triggered` monitor.
- BLO-12852's monitor specifically can be re-armed (or is confirmed cleared) once the fix lands.

## Verifying signal
- Automated test in the paperclip server suite: seed an issue with `executionState.monitor.status = "triggered"`, `nextCheckAt = null`, `attemptCount = 18`; PATCH a monitor with a future `nextCheckAt`; assert **either** the row reflects the new `nextCheckAt`/`notes`, **or** the response is non-2xx with a reason string. Assert specifically that a `200`-with-unchanged-row outcome fails the test — that is the exact bug.
- Manual confirmation: re-arm the monitor on [BLO-12852](/BLO/issues/BLO-12852) and re-read the issue, showing `monitorNextCheckAt` non-null; paste both the request and the post-write read into a comment here.
